newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australian bonds nudging range peaks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australian bonds nudging range peaks.

text.p: *Australian bond futures ended afterhours trading with modest gains, underpinned by a stable U.S. Treasury market despite a strong NAPM index.
*Q1 foreign debt data delayed until June 4.
Australian bond futures ended after hours trading with modest gains, underpinned by a stable U.S. Treasury market, despite a strong U.S. National Association Purchasing Management index.
The June 10-year bond futures contract ended SYCOM at 92.630, just below a fresh 3-1/2 month high of 92.640, and up from Monday's 92.610 close.

The contract dipped to 92.600 at one stage in knee-jerk reaction to a jump in the May NAPM index to 57.1 compared with 54.2 in April, but this level proved supportive and is expected to provide the base for ranging trading up to 92.670.

Analysts said a break of 92.670 takes the market into a heavy resistance area all the way up to the psychological 92.750 level, while a break to the downside through 92.600 should find further support at 92.550.
No local data will be released on Tuesday with first quarter foreign debt data now delayed until Wednesday, at the same time as the first quarter national accounts are issued.
Median forecasts centre on 0.8 percent quarter GDP rise compared with 0.5 percent growth in the December quarter, according to a Reuters survey of economists.
The annual rate of growth will drop to 2.2 percent from 3.1 percent in the previous quarter as a large rise in the March quarter 1996 drops out.
The Reserve Bank of Australia holds its monthly board meeting today, although a further change in policy so soon after the surprise 1/2 point cut to 5.5 percent on May 23 is generally seen unlikely.
However, Reuters monthly interest rate poll of economists found the median percentage chance of another rate cut this cycle at 35 percent.
